name: select
purpose: Select control for choosing one (`multiple={false}`) or many (`multiple={true}`) options from a list. The trigger field mirrors `Input`'s visual API (size, hover/focus/filled/disabled/invalid/required states) so a Select sits next to a TextInput without visual drift. The dropdown panel is teleported to `body` and anchored to the trigger by the shared `usePlacement` composable — no `@floating-ui` runtime. Each option carries a radio indicator in single mode or a checkbox indicator in multi mode, optionally a leading slot/icon and a trailing tag. Search and "Create new" footer are exposed as slots on `<SelectContent>`. Aligned with Figma frames `3714:10801` (trigger states) and `3899:29361` (options panel).
useWhen: One value from a list too long to show inline (regions, runtimes, plans).
Options grouped under headings, with icons or trailing tags.
A list that needs a search box or a "Create new" action inside the panel.
avoidWhen: A select with a visible label and helper/error text in a form → put it inside a `field`; the trigger picks up the field's id, description and state.
The field is always multi-pick → use `multi-select`.
Two to five options that fit on screen → use horizontal `field`s with a `radio-button`, or `radio-cards` for cards.
The list triggers actions or navigation instead of holding a value → use `dropdown`.
related: field` — label, this select, and description/error, with the wiring done.
multi-select` — multi-only variant with checkbox rows and an array model.
dropdown` — action menu that reports the chosen option as an event and holds no form value.
input-group` — joins a select to an input, such as currency plus amount.
bestPractices: Render `Select.Trigger` and `Select.Content` inside the root; the parts read the root's context and throw outside it.
Give each `Select.Option` a stable `value`; pass `displayValue` to control how the trigger renders the selection.

Type an options list as `SelectOptionItem<string>[]` and render it with `v-for` into `Select.Option` (`:value`, `:icon`, `:disabled`, the `label` as the slot); bind a typed model so `displayValue` and `update:modelValue` take that type with no cast.
With `multiple`, `modelValue` becomes an array; for a field that is always multi-pick prefer `multi-select`.
Use `readonly` to show a fixed selection and `disabled` when the field is unavailable; neither opens the panel.

A switcher inside a line of text, such as the environment that ends a resource's breadcrumb (`Workloads › workload_01 › Production ⌄`), is `kind="transparent"` with `size="small"` and an `aria-label` on `Select.Trigger`: no border or fill until hover, sized to its value. Never put a bordered field in the header, and never restyle the trigger with `!` overrides.
Keep `kind="transparent"` out of forms: it draws no border, so it cannot show the `invalid` or `required` border; a form field is the default `outlined` inside a `Field`.

props.name: multiple
props.doc: When true, switches the component to multi-select; options render checkbox indicators and `modelValue` is an array.

props.name: placeholder
props.doc: Trigger placeholder shown when no option is selected.

props.name: size
props.doc: Size token; affects trigger height (small=28px, medium=32px, large=40px) matching `Input`.

props.name: kind
props.doc: Trigger look: `outlined` is the bordered field; `transparent` has no border or fill until hover, sized to its value, for a switcher inside a line of text such as the environment at the end of a breadcrumb.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Disables the trigger and prevents opening; applies disabled tokens.

props.name: readonly
props.doc: Marks the field read-only; the current selection is visible but the dropdown cannot open.

props.name: required
props.doc: Marks the field as required; applies the required (warning) border and sets `aria-required` on the trigger, matching `Input`. The label's Required tag is owned by the wrapping form-field, not by this component.

props.name: invalid
props.doc: Applies the invalid border + ring tokens and sets `aria-invalid` on the trigger.

props.name: displayValue
props.doc: Custom formatter used by the trigger to render the selected label(s); receives the current `modelValue`, typed as the bound model.

slots.name: default
slots.notes: Composition slot; receives `<SelectTrigger>` and `<SelectContent>` (and the option tree inside it).

examples.name: Default
examples.sfc:
<script setup>
  import Select from '@aziontech/webkit/select'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const value = ref('')
  const options = [
    { value: 'opt-1', label: 'Option 1' },
    { value: 'opt-2', label: 'Option 2' },
    { value: 'opt-3', label: 'Option 3' },
    { value: 'opt-4', label: 'Option 4' }
  ]
</script>

<template>
  <Select
    aria-label="Option"
    v-model="value"
    size="large"
    placeholder="Select an option"
  >
    <Select.Trigger />
    <Select.Content>
      <Select.Option
        v-for="o in options"
        :key="o.value"
        :value="o.value"
        >{{ o.label }}</Select.Option
      >
    </Select.Content>
  </Select>
</template>
